title: Hooks evaluate array operands that Go leaves unevaluated
claim: Wrapping concat or slicing inside constant len/cap or an unevaluated array range inserts a function call that changes Go's evaluation decision. Valid const and array-length expressions stop compiling, while len([1]string{s[:high]}) and for range [1]string{s[:high]} newly panic for an out-of-range high even with IAST disabled.
repro_command: cd /tmp/ddiast-review/wt/hooks-yml-operators && REVIEW_WOVEN=1 GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 GOFLAGS=-p=2 DD_IAST_ENABLED=false go tool orchestrion go test -work -timeout 3m -count=1 -v ./reviewoperators ./reviewoperators/constantlen ./reviewoperators/floatbounds ./reviewoperators/noimports

title: Integral floating-point and complex slice bounds stop compiling
claim: Valid slice bounds 1.0, 3.0, and complex(1, 0) become float64 or complex128 generic arguments and fail the integer constraint. The matcher's untyped exclusion is ineffective because go/types has already assigned int to the original index expressions. Both string and full byte slicing fail.
repro_command: cd /tmp/ddiast-review/wt/hooks-yml-operators && GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 go tool orchestrion go test -timeout 3m -count=1 ./reviewoperators/floatbounds

title: Operator instrumentation crashes the weaver on import-free packages
claim: The operator aspects add propagation imports to previously import-free root packages. The pinned weaver leaves PackageFile nil when parsing an empty importcfg, then assigns the injected dependency into it at oncompile.go:195. An ordinary string-helper package fails to build with panic: assignment to entry in nil map.
repro_command: cd /tmp/ddiast-review/wt/hooks-yml-operators && GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 go tool orchestrion go test -timeout 3m -count=1 ./reviewoperators/noimports

title: Disabled operator wrappers force avoidable heap allocations
claim: With DD_IAST_ENABLED=false and HasValues false, len(a+b), a+b comparison, and a locally assigned string(byteSlice) used only by len each allocate once per operation after weaving versus zero natively. Retaining propagation-capable helper calls change escape behavior before the activity gate can avoid the allocation. Direct comparison and map-key conversion controls stay allocation-free.
repro_command: cd /tmp/ddiast-review/wt/hooks-yml-operators && REVIEW_WOVEN=1 GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 DD_IAST_ENABLED=false go tool orchestrion go test -timeout 3m -count=1 -v -run 'Test(WeavingPreflight|InactiveAllocations)' ./reviewoperators
